## Why
The first 81-case pilot used a common angular amplitude. The user asked to treat matter and radiation anisotropic stresses independently, including cases that initially cancel. Adding component norms would lose that cancellation.

## What changed
- Add an independent signed 9×9×9 initial grid in Sigma, Pi_m and Pi_r: **729 completed cases, 243 successful groups, 47,385 stored states**.
- Retain the unchanged REI C15 owner at `80825585f9fe31d2ee0d5af545ada3fa1f52be72`. Split execution source is BASS `82372ed8db68085868603d4267a630ed9cde6abb`.
- Matter means the existing massive nonbaryonic Vlasov species; isotropic gas/cold matter have zero anisotropic stress. Radiation includes photons, massless neutrinos and evolving UV.
- Form the tensor sum before its norm. Preserve component/total signed values, half-contraction and Frobenius norms, work and cancellation diagnostics.
- Reuse readonly preparation within three-case groups. The shared executor admits work from actual available CPU/RAM, uses one numerical thread per worker and verifies hashes before reusing completed groups.

## Actual result
For initial signed (Sigma, Pi_m, Pi_r) = (0, +4e-4, -4e-4), the final signed total stress is **-1.91763629195e-7** and signed shear **-4.79541095495e-11**. The opposite sign seed gives the opposite response. Independent component evolution breaks initial cancellation.

Two actual-data figures show separate component changes and shear response relative to the same-initial-Sigma zero-stress control. Full raw values remain available.

## Validation and scope
243 PASS receipts; the expanded invocation reused the first group and completed 242 new groups. All 5,832 stored numerical gates passed. Independent review matched 3,450,357 raw/CSV scalars, checked 2,662,299 finite JSON floats, tensor/work normalization and final figure provenance.

This is a **warm a=0.1999→0.2, non-tilted LRS conditional pilot**, not a full cold-EoR history, general non-LRS model, full emitter/escape Q^a closure or convergence claim. Thermochemical effects are not resolved. No new detailed performance benchmark or speedup claim.

The actual new run used the current 8-CPU/8-GiB profile with up to eight workers. NCP 64-CPU/128-GiB resource-aware settings are ready; this environment lacks the previously authorized SSH key, so no new NCP execution is claimed.
